jobs.name: v1_walk
jobs.prompt: The black basalt hound in the picture walks forward to the left at a calm, steady pace across a long floor, seen exactly from the side. It faces left and travels to the left in exact side profile. Natural four-beat dog walk: each paw stays firmly planted on the floor while it carries weight, then lifts, swings forward and lands in front; the legs on one side move one after the other, hind leg first, then front leg. Head and neck bob gently with each step, the iron collar and its hanging rings swing, the tail is relaxed and sways. The hound never turns, never walks toward or away from the camera, never walks backwards. Its paws stay sharp and solid where they touch the floor. The camera tracks sideways with the hound at its speed, so it stays in the centre of the picture, always fully visible from nose to tail tip, while the floor joint lines slide past. Smooth tracking shot at constant height and distance, no zoom, no cuts, plain light grey studio background, even soft lighting, the same hound and the same size throughout.

jobs.name: v5_death
jobs.prompt: The black basalt hound in the picture stands facing left in exact side profile, seen exactly from the side. It is struck by a fatal blow from the front: it flinches back, staggers, its hind legs buckle and give way, then its front legs fold, and it collapses heavily onto the floor and rolls onto its right side, so its left flank with the glowing brand mark faces up toward the camera side. It lies still with legs limp, head down on the floor, a last small twitch of the tail, then no motion. The iron collar and its hanging rings fall and settle. It never turns its head or body toward or away from the camera. The camera stays steady at the same height and distance and keeps the whole hound centred and fully visible from nose to tail tip at all times, no zoom, no cuts, plain light grey studio background, even soft lighting, the same hound and the same size throughout.

jobs.name: v7_death_b
jobs.prompt: One continuous shot without any cut: the black basalt hound in the picture stands facing left in exact side profile, seen exactly from the side. It is hit by a fatal blow from the front: it flinches back and staggers one step, its hind legs buckle, then its front legs fold, and its whole body sinks down and tips over sideways, falling heavily onto its right side on the floor, with its legs ending toward the camera and its head on the floor at the left. It lies still on its side, legs limp and slightly bent, the tail gives one last small twitch, then nothing moves. The iron collar and its hanging rings fall and settle. The whole fall takes about three seconds, then it lies still for the rest of the video. The camera stays fixed at the same height, distance and angle for the entire video, always showing the whole hound from nose to tail tip, no zoom, no cuts, no jumps in time, plain light grey studio background, even soft lighting, the same hound and the same size throughout.
